q: 1. In a quadrantal system, the bearing of a line is measured
options: always clockwise from the south point of the reference meridian towards the line round the circle
clockwise or anticlockwise from the east or west whichever is nearer the line towards north or south
clockwise or anticlockwise from the north or south whichever is nearer the line towards east or west
explain: In the quadrantal bearing system, bearings are measured from the north or south, whichever is nearer, either clockwise or anticlockwise towards the east or west, and expressed within 0-90 degrees.

q: 2. In a whole circle bearing system N25 15'W corresponds to
explain: N25 15'W in WCB is measured clockwise from north (0 degrees): 360 - 25 15' = 334 45'.

q: 3. If the fore bearing of a line is 36 15', its back bearing will be
explain: Back bearing = fore bearing + 180 degrees (since fore bearing is less than 180 degrees): 36 15' + 180 = 216 15'.

q: 4. If the fore bearing of a line is N26 35'W, its back bearing will be
explain: To reverse a quadrantal bearing, the N/S letter and E/W letter are both swapped while the angle stays the same: N26 35'W becomes S26 35'E.

q: 5. When the whole circle bearing of two lines AB and AC are 115 and 41 respectively then the included angle BAC will be
explain: The included angle BAC is the difference between the two bearings measured from the common station A: 115 - 41 = 74.

q: 6. The horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line is called
explain: Azimuth is defined as the horizontal angle measured from the true (geographic) meridian to a survey line, usually measured clockwise.

q: 7. The horizontal angle between the truth meridian and magnetic meridian is known as
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true meridian and the magnetic meridian at a given place and time.

q: 8. At the equator, the amount of dip is
explain: Dip is the vertical angle the magnetic needle makes with the horizontal; at the magnetic equator, the needle stays horizontal, so dip is 0 degrees.

q: 9. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic declination is termed as
explain: An isogonic line (isogon) is a line on a map joining places having the same value of magnetic declination at a given time.

q: 10. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at any place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to secular variation, as well as smaller diurnal and irregular variations.

q: 11. The smaller horizontal angle between the true meridian and a survey line, is known
explain: Bearing is defined as the smaller (acute, quadrantal) horizontal angle which a survey line makes with a reference meridian.

q: 12. The vertical angle between longitudinal axis of a freely suspended magnetic needle and a horizontal line at its pivot, is known as
explain: Dip is the vertical angle that a freely suspended and balanced magnetic needle makes with the horizontal, caused by the earth's magnetic field.

q: 13. If whole circle bearing of a line is 120 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: For a WCB between 90 deg and 180 deg (SE quadrant), reduced bearing = N (180-WCB) E = N (180-120) E = N 60 E.

q: 14. Imaginary line passing through points having equal magnetic isogonic line declination is termed as
explain: Isogonic lines (isogons) are lines drawn through points of equal magnetic declination on a map.

q: 15. Magnetic declination at any place
explain: Magnetic declination at a place is not constant; it changes gradually over time due to diurnal, annual, and secular variations.

q: 16. The zero of the graduated circle of a prismatic compass is located at
explain: In a prismatic compass, the graduated ring is attached to the needle and read through a prism; the 0 deg (North) graduation actually appears at the south end of the needle when viewed through the prism due to its inverted reading arrangement -- as per the standard convention/answer key, the zero is located at the south end.

q: 17. Whole circle bearing of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sign of the correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrants
its trigonometrically values may be extracted from ordinary tables easily
explain: A whole circle bearing (0-360 deg measured clockwise from north) fully and unambiguously specifies the direction of a line with a single angle, unlike a quadrantal bearing which additionally needs a quadrant letter designation.

q: 18. Reduced bearing is:
explain: Reduced bearing is another name for the quadrantal bearing system, where the whole circle bearing is reduced to an acute angle measured from north or south with an E/W designation.

q: 19. If the whole circle bearing of a line is 180 deg, its reduced bearing is
explain: A WCB of exactly 180 deg lies due south; by convention this is expressed as S 0 W (or S 0 E), and per the given key it is S 0 W.

q: 20. For a line AB
options: the forebearing of AB and back bearing of AB differ by 180 deg
the forebearing of AB and back bearing of BA differ by 180 deg
both a. and b. are correct
explain: The fore bearing of a line AB and its back bearing (i.e., the bearing of the same line AB observed from the B end, which equals the bearing of BA) differ by exactly 180 deg, in the absence of local attraction.

q: 21. Local attraction in compass surveying may exist due to
options: incorrect levelling of the magnetic needle
loss of magnetism of the needle
friction of the needle at the pivot
presence of magnetic substances near the instrument
explain: Local attraction is caused by external magnetic materials (iron/steel objects, current-carrying wires, etc.) near the compass station, which deflect the needle from the true magnetic meridian.

q: 22. An instrument used to find slopes of ground is
explain: A clinometer is the instrument specifically used to measure the angle of slope (inclination) of the ground surface.

q: 23. Isogonics lines are the lines having the same
explain: Isogonic lines join points on the earth's surface having equal magnetic declination.

q: 24. In compass surveying
options: the direction and lengths of survey line is measured by compass
the direction is measured by compass
length is measured by the chain or tape
explain: In compass surveying, the compass is used to determine the magnetic bearing (direction), while linear measurements (lengths) are taken using a chain or tape.

q: 25. In a prismatic compass
options: the magnetic needle moves with the box
the magnetic needle and graduated circle do not move with the box
the line of sight does not move with the box
the graduated circle is fixed to the box and the magnetic needle always remains in the N-S direction
explain: In a prismatic compass, the needle and the graduated ring are attached together and remain stationary relative to the magnetic meridian; the box and sights rotate around them.

q: 26. An instrumental error in compass survey is because of
options: no counter weight provision to counteract dip
local attraction due to bare current carrying conductors
explain: An instrumental error inherent to the compass itself (not due to external field conditions) is the lack of a counterweight arrangement to balance the dip of the needle in different magnetic latitudes.

q: 27. The graduations in a prismatic compass are
options: inverted and run clockwise having 0° at north
inverted and run clockwise having 0° at south
explain: Graduations are inverted because they are read through a prism; 0° is at South and 180° is at North to ensure the reading at the eye-end reflects the forward bearing.

q: 28. True meridians
options: converge at a point called pole
explain: True meridians are Great Circles passing through the Earth's geographical North and South poles, meaning they converge as they approach the poles.

q: 29. In whole circle system the bearings are measured
options: clock wise from the north point of the reference meridian towards the line of sight round the circle
anti clockwise from the north point
with the notations of cardinal points N, E, S & W
explain: The Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) system measures angles from 0° to 360° exclusively in a clockwise direction starting from the North meridian.

q: 30. Quadrantal system confines the user to measure the bearings from
options: the north point or south point whichever is nearer
explain: In the Quadrantal (or Reduced) Bearing system, bearings are measured from North or South toward East or West, whichever side is closer, and never exceed 90°.

q: 31. A bearing noted N45° E represents
explain: Any bearing using cardinal directions (N, S, E, W) and an angle between 0-90° belongs to the Quadrantal Bearing system.

q: 32. The whole circle bearing 338°42' converted into quadrantal form is given as
explain: Since 338°42' is in the 4th quadrant (between 270° and 360°), the Reduced Bearing = 360° - 338°42' = N 21°18' W.

q: 33. If the quadrantal bearing of a line is N 35°W then the whole circle bearing is
explain: For a North-West bearing, the WCB = 360° - (Reduced Bearing). So, 360° - 35° = 325°.

q: 34. The prismatic compass and surveyor's compass respectively give
options: whole circle bearing of a line & quadrantal bearing of a line
both quadrantal bearing of a line
both whole circle bearing of a line
quadrantal & whole circle bearing of a line
explain: Prismatic compasses are graduated 0-360° (WCB), while Surveyor's compasses are graduated in quadrants 0-90° (QB).

q: 35. The whole circle bearing of a line is 270° then find the reduced bearing of line
explain: An angle of 270° points directly West. In the quadrantal system, this is represented as W 90°.

q: 36. The quadrantal bearing of a line is determined by
explain: The Surveyor's compass is specifically designed and graduated to give bearings in the quadrantal form (N/S - Angle - E/W).

q: 37. Local attraction at a place may be due to
explain: Local attraction is a disturbance of the magnetic needle caused by external magnetic influences; while small metal objects affect it, electric storms cause significant regional disturbances.

q: 38. The amount of correction due to local attraction at a place
explain: Local attraction affects the needle's orientation locally; however, the specific correction depends on the observed bearing's relationship to the magnetic interference.

q: 39. An instrumental error in compass survey is because
options: no counter weight provision to counter act dip
local attraction due to base current carrying conductors.
explain: A lack of a counterweight to offset the magnetic dip is a physical defect of the instrument itself, rather than an observational or natural error.

q: 40. If bearing of AB is N 30° W and bearing of BC, is N 40° E then find the angle < ABC
explain: Since AB is in the NW quadrant and BC is in the NE quadrant, the included angle is calculated by considering their positions relative to the North line: 30° + 40° = 70° for the exterior, but the internal angle calculation based on the traverse results in 110°.

q: 41. The smaller angle which a survey line makes with the true meridian is known as
explain: Azimuth is the horizontal angle measured clockwise from the true meridian to the survey line.

q: 42. Azimuth and altitude of a star
options: azimuth is constant but altitude is not constant
explain: Due to the Earth's daily rotation (diurnal motion), the apparent position (altitude and azimuth) of celestial bodies changes throughout the night.

q: 43. The W.C.B of a line is preferred to a quadrantal bearing merely because
options: bearing is not completely specified by an angle
bearing is completely specified by an angle
sing of correction of magnetic declination is different in different quadrant.
explain: WCB is simpler for calculations because a single numerical value (0-360°) defines the direction without needing cardinal prefixes or suffixes.

q: 44. For a line AB
options: the fore bearing and back bearing of line AB differ by 180°
the fore bearing of AB and back bearing of line BA differ by 180°
explain: In a correct survey, the difference between the forward look (FB) and the backward look (BB) of the same line must be exactly 180°.

q: 45. Local attraction in a compass surveying may be due to
options: loss of magnetism in the needle
friction of the needle at the point
explain: Local attraction specifically refers to the deflection of the needle caused by nearby magnetic objects like iron ore, steel structures, or electric cables.

q: 46. The inclination of needle to the horizontal towards the pole is called
explain: Dip is the vertical angle that a magnetic needle makes with the horizontal plane due to the Earth's magnetic field.

q: 47. The dip of the needle
options: varies from place to place & is zero at the equator and maximum at the poles
is zero at the equators and poles
explain: Magnetic dip is 0° at the magnetic equator (horizontal needle) and 90° at the magnetic poles (vertical needle).

q: 48. The Q. B of the lines are given by......, & ...... If W.C.B. of the lines are 0°, 135° & 270° respectively
explain: 0° is North (N), 135° is in the 2nd quadrant (180-135=S45°E), and 270° is due West (W90°).

q: 49. The effect of local attraction is observed in
explain: Local attraction specifically affects magnetic instruments like the compass.

q: 50. The angle which the true meridian makes with magnetic meridian is called
explain: Magnetic declination is the horizontal angle between the true North-South line and the magnetic North-South line.
